tool.name: KIR genes
tool.description: gene content, alleles, A/B genotype and B content from exome reads with T1K
tool.command: ln -s '$bam' input.bam && ln -s '${bam.metadata.bam_index}' input.bam.bai && python3 '$__tool_directory__/wes_kir.py' --bam input.bam #if $kir_dat: --kir-dat '$kir_dat' #end if #if $hla: --hla '$hla' #end if --sample '$bam.element_identifier' --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} --min-quality $min_quality --min-abundance $min_abundance --tsv '$genes' --json '$summary'

param.name: bam
param.label: Aligned reads (BAM)
param.help: Duplicate-marked reads of the sample, aligned to GRCh38 (19 or chr19), with the unmapped reads.

param.name: kir_dat
param.label: KIR alleles (IPD-KIR kir.dat)
param.help: kir.dat of an IPD-KIR release (https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/ipd/kir/, CC BY-ND 4.0). Without it nothing is typed.

param.name: hla
param.label: HLA types (wes_hla summary)
param.help: The summary of the HLA typing tool (wes_hla 0.2 or later): the KIR ligand groups of the HLA-A, -B and -C alleles (C1/C2, Bw4).

param.name: min_quality
param.label: Lowest T1K quality of a present gene
param.help: 0: any allele T1K calls (the tuning showed no gain from a quality cut-off).

param.name: min_abundance
param.label: Lowest abundance of a present gene, as a fraction of the framework genes' mean

tool.help:
**What it does**
Types the killer-cell immunoglobulin-like receptor (KIR) genes from the exome reads with T1K 1.0.10 (Song et al., Genome Research 2023; MIT) against the IPD-KIR database. In each job it builds T1K's allele reference from ``kir.dat`` (about 2 s), takes the reads of the KIR region (chromosome 19, 54.6-55.0 Mb) and the unmapped reads, and runs T1K with its exome preset. A KIR haplotype has 4 to 14 genes and the reference genome only one haplotype, so reads of the other genes map to their paralogues or not at all; T1K assigns them to the alleles of all 17 KIR genes.
**Gene content.** A gene is present when T1K calls an allele of it with an abundance of at least 10 % of the framework genes' mean (KIR3DL3, KIR3DP1, KIR2DL4, KIR3DL2, present on nearly every haplotype); both cut-offs were set on half of a 1000 Genomes panel and checked on the other half against the same people's genomes (README section 7). Alleles are given at three digits (protein level); copy number is not determined.
**From the gene content**: the A/B genotype (AA: only genes of the A haplotype), the centromeric and telomeric motifs, and the B-content group used to choose unrelated donors for patients with acute myeloid leukaemia (Cooley et al., Blood 2010: Best = Cen-B/B; Better = two or more B motifs; Neutral otherwise). With the HLA summary of wes_hla: the KIR-HLA ligand pairs (KIR2DL1-C2, KIR2DL2/3-C1, KIR3DL1-Bw4, KIR2DS1-C2, KIR3DS1-Bw4-80I).
**Outputs**: a table of the 17 genes (present, alleles, quality, abundance relative to the framework genes) and a JSON summary for the clinical report.
